200-### Edge Cases
201-
202-- **Duplicate on edit and import**: Editing an address to match another bookmark, or importing an address that already exists, is resolved to the existing bookmark rather than creating a duplicate (per User Story 2).
203:- **Address normalization ambiguity**: Two addresses that look different but resolve to the same resource (trailing slash, host case, default port, tracking parameters) are treated as duplicates; genuinely different paths/queries are kept separate. Exact rules are in Assumptions.
204-- **Metadata fetch failures/timeouts**: The bookmark is still created from the address; the user is told metadata was unavailable and can retry.
205-- **Very long titles/descriptions/notes or unusual characters**: Stored fully and displayed without breaking layout (truncated in the list with full content available on the detail view).
206-- **Malformed search query**: Unbalanced quotes/parentheses or a dangling operator yield a clear message, not misleading results.

211-- **Restoring an archived item that was in read-later or had read state**: Its prior read-later membership and read/unread state are retained on restore.
212-- **Import of malformed file**: Valid entries import; invalid entries are reported with a summary.
213-- **Preserving a page that requires login or is unreachable**: Preservation fails gracefully with a clear message; the bookmark is unaffected.
214:- **PDF vs. web page detection**: A destination identified as a PDF is preserved as a PDF; otherwise a self-contained HTML copy of the page is stored.
215-- **Empty states**: First-time (no bookmarks), empty read-later, empty archive, and no-result searches/filters each show a friendly empty state.
216-- **Formatting in notes**: Only simple, safe formatting is rendered; any unsupported or unsafe markup is neutralized when displayed.

298-### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
299-
300-- **Bookmark**: A saved link. Attributes: address, title, description, note (formatted), site icon, preview image, tags, creation timestamp, last-updated timestamp, read-later flag, read/unread state, archive state, and references to any preserved local copy and Internet Archive snapshot.
301:- **Tag**: A short label grouping bookmarks. Many-to-many with bookmarks; existing tags are suggested during entry. Tag names are unique within the collection (case-insensitive); the same name always refers to a single tag.
302-- **Saved Search**: A named, reusable combination of a search query plus included and excluded tags.
303:- **Preserved Copy**: A stored local rendition of a page — a self-contained HTML file representing the original page, or a PDF when the source is a PDF — and/or a reference to an Internet Archive snapshot, associated with a bookmark.
304-- **Display Preferences**: Per-user settings for default sort order, items shown, and text size.

306-## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
--
320-
321-- **Single user, no login, one device to start**: v1 is a single-user personal collection with no accounts; cross-device sync is deferred (client-confirmed).
322-- **Web application**: Delivered as a browser-based web app per the project's runtime presentation environment; a server-side component is expected because metadata fetching, page preservation, Internet Archive submission, and import/export exceed what a browser page can do purely client-side. (Concrete technology chosen at the plan gate.)
323:- **Address normalization rules for deduplication (v1)**: addresses are compared as duplicates only when they are safely equivalent. Normalization is limited to lower-casing the host (site name) and ignoring a default port. Trailing slashes and query/tracking parameters are NOT removed, because they can lead to genuinely different pages; any such difference keeps bookmarks distinct. These rules can be refined later.
324-- **Metadata source**: title, description, and preview image are taken from standard page metadata (e.g., Open Graph / standard meta tags) with the site favicon as the icon; a best-effort fallback is used when those are absent.
325-- **Note formatting**: "simple formatting" means a lightweight rich-text/markdown-style set (bold, italic, lists, links, headings) rendered safely; full HTML authoring is out of scope.
326-- **Standard bookmark file format**: import/export uses the widely supported Netscape bookmark HTML format used by major browsers; folder names map to tags on import.
327:- **Page preservation scope (v1)**: a preserved web page is stored best-effort as a single self-contained HTML file representing the original page (embedding the resources needed to display it), not merely an extracted readable version; a destination that is a PDF is stored as a PDF. It does not guarantee capture of login-gated pages, streamed media, or highly dynamic app states. Internet Archive preservation depends on that external service being reachable.
328:- **Search operator precedence**: NOT binds tightest, then AND, then OR, with parentheses overriding; case-insensitive; unquoted multi-word terms are treated as separate ANDed keywords unless quoted.
329-- **Standard error handling**: invalid input and failed external operations produce user-friendly messages with no data loss.
330-- **External dependencies**: automatic metadata, page preservation, and Internet Archive submission require outbound network access to the target sites and to the Internet Archive; these may be unavailable in restricted environments and degrade gracefully.
